reasoning: OSU Micro-Benchmarks 5.8 is a real MPI communication benchmark. The :libfabric variant is an amd64 OpenMPI 4.1.2 build explicitly configured against libfabric with the OFI MTL (mca_mtl_ofi.so, libfabric.so.1.24.0), so it can drive a fast OFI/EFA fabric and still fall back to TCP over ethernet — the best choice for a 5-node run. Other variants are either arch-specific (hpc7g/arm64), profiling-instrumented (vtune), vendor-stack-bound (azure-hpc HPC-X/MVAPICH2), or plain builds with no OFI path. The CUDA-enabled HPC-X variant is unnecessary since this is the CPU benchmark set, so needs_gpu is false. At 5 nodes a point-to-point test (osu_latency/osu_bw) would only use 2 ranks, so I selected osu_allreduce, a collective that scales across all ranks on all 5 nodes, sweeping 8B–1MB messages to exercise both latency- and bandwidth-bound regimes. Network is efa OR ethernet so the job can match either fabric. Memory is 0-16GB: OSU allocates only small per-rank send/recv buffers (max 1MB here), so even a small node cannot OOM.
